concepts.title: The Emergence of Nationalism and Early Political Associations

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Emergence of Nationalism and Early Political Associations' refers to.
questions.a: The development of a shared consciousness among Indians that India belonged to all its people, leading to the formation of political associations to challenge British control over the nation's resources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Emergence of Nationalism and Early Political Associations'.
questions.a: The realization that India's resources and systems belonged to its diverse population, not the British rulers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Emergence of Nationalism and Early Political Associations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Emergence of Nationalism (source: hess208.txt lines 15-50)

concepts.title: British Repressive Measures of the 1870s and 1880s

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'British Repressive Measures of the 1870s and 1880s' refers to.
questions.a: A series of legislative acts passed by the British administration, including the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act, which restricted Indian freedoms and fueled national discontent.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'British Repressive Measures of the 1870s and 1880s'.
questions.a: Repressive British laws like the Arms Act, Vernacular Press Act, and the withdrawal of the Ilbert Bill intensified Indian dissatisfaction.

questions.q: Under which section is 'British Repressive Measures of the 1870s and 1880s' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Emergence of Nationalism (source: hess208.txt lines 51-70)

concepts.title: Establishment of the Indian National Congress

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Establishment of the Indian National Congress' refers to.
questions.a: The formation of an all-India political organization in December 1885 at Bombay, bringing together representatives from different regions to voice national demands.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Establishment of the Indian National Congress'.
questions.a: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by 72 delegates to provide a unified platform for educated Indians.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Establishment of the Indian National Congress' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Emergence of Nationalism (source: hess208.txt lines 71-95)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Moderate Phase of the Congress' refers to.
questions.a: The initial twenty years of the Indian National Congress characterized by peaceful methods, constitutional demands, and raising awareness about the economic drain of India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Moderate Phase of the Congress'.
questions.a: Moderates sought administrative reforms, greater representation, and highlighted the economic ruin caused by British rule.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Moderate Phase of the Congress' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A nation in the making (source: hess208.txt lines 96-145)

concepts.title: The Rise of Radical Politics and the Partition of Bengal

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Rise of Radical Politics and the Partition of Bengal' refers to.
questions.a: The emergence of a more assertive leadership within the Congress that advocated self-reliance, opposed the 1905 partition of Bengal, and initiated the Swadeshi movement.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Rise of Radical Politics and the Partition of Bengal'.
questions.a: Radicals like Lal-Bal-Pal rejected the 'politics of prayers' and led the mass protest against the partition of Bengal.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Rise of Radical Politics and the Partition of Bengal' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: "Freedom is our birthright" (source: hess208.txt lines 146-190)

concepts.title: Early Twentieth Century Political Developments and Splits

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Early Twentieth Century Political Developments and Splits' refers to.
questions.a: Key political events between 1906 and 1916, including the formation of the Muslim League, the Surat split of the Congress, and their subsequent reunion and alliance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Early Twentieth Century Political Developments and Splits'.
questions.a: The formation of the Muslim League, the 1907 Congress split, and the 1916 Lucknow Pact shaped early nationalist alignments.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Early Twentieth Century Political Developments and Splits' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: "Freedom is our birthright" (source: hess208.txt lines 191-215)

concepts.title: Economic and Political Impact of the First World War

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic and Political Impact of the First World War' refers to.
questions.a: The profound changes brought by the global conflict of 1914-1918, which altered India's economic landscape, expanded local industries, and created widespread discontent.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic and Political Impact of the First World War'.
questions.a: The First World War led to high taxes, rising prices, industrial expansion, and a new anti-colonial consciousness among returning soldiers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Economic and Political Impact of the First World War' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Growth of Mass Nationalism (source: hess208.txt lines 216-245)

concepts.title: The Advent of Mahatma Gandhi and Early Satyagrahas

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Advent of Mahatma Gandhi and Early Satyagrahas' refers to.
questions.a: The return of Mahatma Gandhi from South Africa in 1915 and his initial localized non-violent struggles in Champaran, Kheda, and Ahmedabad.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Advent of Mahatma Gandhi and Early Satyagrahas'.
questions.a: Gandhiji emerged as a respected leader, applying non-violent satyagraha to local peasant and worker grievances.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Advent of Mahatma Gandhi and Early Satyagrahas' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The advent of Mahatma Gandhi (source: hess208.txt lines 246-270)

concepts.title: The Rowlatt Satyagraha and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Rowlatt Satyagraha and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre' refers to.
questions.a: The first nation-wide protest campaign launched by Gandhiji in 1919 against repressive British legislation, which was met with brutal state violence in Amritsar.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Rowlatt Satyagraha and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre'.
questions.a: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was a unified struggle against the curbing of basic freedoms, marked by the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Rowlatt Satyagraha and Jallianwala Bagh Massacre' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Rowlatt Satyagraha (source: hess208.txt lines 271-305)

concepts.title: The Khilafat Agitation and Non-Cooperation Movement

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Khilafat Agitation and Non-Cooperation Movement' refers to.
questions.a: A major joint mass movement launched in 1920 combining Muslim anger over the treatment of the Turkish Khalifa with Indian demands for Swaraj and justice for Punjab wrongs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Khilafat Agitation and Non-Cooperation Movement'.
questions.a: The alliance of the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements created unprecedented Hindu-Muslim unity and mass mobilization.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Khilafat Agitation and Non-Cooperation Movement' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Khilafat agitation and the Non-Cooperation Movement (source: hess208.txt lines 306-345)

concepts.title: People's Initiatives and Local Interpretations of Satyagraha

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'People's Initiatives and Local Interpretations of Satyagraha' refers to.
questions.a: The diverse ways in which different social classes, peasants, and tribals interpreted Gandhiji's message to address their own local grievances, sometimes deviating from non-violence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'People's Initiatives and Local Interpretations of Satyagraha'.
questions.a: Ordinary people often viewed Gandhiji as a messiah and linked his name to local struggles against landlords and forest laws.

questions.q: Under which section is 'People's Initiatives and Local Interpretations of Satyagraha' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: People's initiatives (source: hess208.txt lines 346-405)

concepts.title: The Happenings of 1922-1929 and Purna Swaraj

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Happenings of 1922-1929 and Purna Swaraj' refers to.
questions.a: The period of transition marked by the withdrawal of Non-Cooperation after the Chauri Chaura incident, constructive work, the Simon Commission boycott, and the resolution for complete independence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Happenings of 1922-1929 and Purna Swaraj'.
questions.a: The decade of the 1920s concluded with the Congress resolving to fight for Purna Swaraj (complete independence) under Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Happenings of 1922-1929 and Purna Swaraj' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The happenings of 1922–1929 (source: hess208.txt lines 406-460)

concepts.title: The Dandi March and the Civil Disobedience Movement

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Dandi March and the Civil Disobedience Movement' refers to.
questions.a: The historic 240-mile march led by Gandhiji in 1930 to break the British salt monopoly, launching a nationwide Civil Disobedience campaign with massive participation, including women.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Dandi March and the Civil Disobedience Movement'.
questions.a: Breaking the salt law united diverse social groups against a basic shared grievance and mobilized women on a large scale.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Dandi March and the Civil Disobedience Movement' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The March to Dandi (source: hess208.txt lines 461-510)

concepts.title: The Quit India Movement and the Path to Partition

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Quit India Movement and the Path to Partition' refers to.
questions.a: The final phase of the freedom struggle launched in 1942 during World War II, followed by negotiations, communal riots, and the eventual partition of the subcontinent in 1947.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Quit India Movement and the Path to Partition'.
questions.a: The 'Do or Die' call of Quit India and the failure of negotiations led to independence accompanied by the tragedy of Partition.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Quit India Movement and the Path to Partition' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Quit India and Later (source: hess208.txt lines 511-600)
